questions: Should the random integers be generated with a uniform distribution, or is any distribution acceptable?
Is the random seed fixed (e.g., np.random.seed(42)) inside the function for reproducibility, or should it be left to default random state?
Should the output array be 1D (shape (10,)) or 2D (shape (10, 1)) as implied by the reference solution?
Is the scaling applied column-wise (default MinMaxScaler behavior) or globally across all values?
Should the function handle edge cases where all random integers are identical (e.g., all zeros)?
Are the random integers inclusive of 0 and exclusive of 10 (i.e., 0 to 9), as typical for np.random.randint?
Should the function return the scaled array as a numpy array of floats, or is integer type acceptable after scaling?
Is the array length fixed at 10 (ARRAY_LENGTH constant), or should it be configurable via a parameter?
